searchText: I cannot speak for other clients, but in Prysm, we will never conflate the following two points: 1) syncing only to the finalized epoch, and 2) syncing to the head of the chain, which is akin to initially missing a block but subsequently discovering it due to attestation. Regarding range verification, it is assumed that the block already exists, which allows for the comparison of the hash tree root. Subsequently, one can verify the blob and the inclusion proof independently Hey folks, I’ve been thinking about the sidecars in the latest modification and it seems to me that’s possible to forge a valid sidecar by simply changing the index in the sidecar, since the index does not affect the proof, the proof will still be valid and therefore the signature too. Is this correct or am I missing something? Either way I think it’s easily solvable by changing the kzg commitment list elements in the beacon block body from just having the kzg commitment to a container having the index and the kzg commitment so the index is included in the root The inclusion proof depends on the index though, as it starts with the neighboring kzg commitment's root Yes but at the moment of verification of a single blob sidecar, we might not have the other blob sidecar to compare this neighboring root attack scenario could be that the signer produces the first blob sidecar with index 0, but also produces equivocating blob sidecars using blob indexes 1 through 5 using the same kzg, the same inclusion proof, and the same signed beacon block header, and then proceeds to release the different blob sidecars to different peers. The last element of the proof is indeed the root of another concealed kzg, but it doesn't matter becuase it has not been broadcasted If we add the index this is impossible I think It might be that the equivocating blob indexes can only be 0, 2 and 4 due to the hashing order (in the case of the indexes 1, 3 and 5 order of hashing is different I think) Ah yes but the order changes also in the rest of the indexes, I think you're right, it might be impossible due to the order 👍 Yes this attack is impossible due to the generalized index changing for each sidecar index, I'll still try to see if I can produce a meaningful test with this in mind 🙂

excerpts.author: terencechain
excerpts.content: I cannot speak for other clients, but in Prysm, we will never conflate the following two points: 1) syncing only to the finalized epoch, and 2) syncing to the head of the chain, which is akin to initially missing a block but subsequently discovering it due to attestation. Regarding range verification, it is assumed that the block already exists, which allows for the comparison of the hash tree root. Subsequently, one can verify the blob and the inclusion proof independently
